reason: 'Stamens staminodal' means these stamens are staminodes, which are sterile, reduced stamens. PO has the class staminode; the other choice, stamen + sterile (PATO_0000956), loses the part.
'Without stolons' states that stolons are absent. It is the opposite of stoloniferous (rule C208).
This is a compound of two existing values, strigose (FLOPO:0991086) and hirsute (FLOPO:0991050). It goes to the continuum pattern, like 'linear-lanceolate', not to a new term.
'Sub-' means almost: weakly denticulate, so finely toothed. Annotate with the approximate-value pattern on PATO dentated (exact synonym toothed).
Means almost hastate, and PATO has hastate. The 'sub-' prefix is handled by the approximate-value pattern, as with suborbicular.
Means almost tongue- or strap-shaped. Two of the three statements are OCR-garbled ('subliiigulalc'); only the style statement is clean, so the mapping is uncertain.
Means almost stellate. PATO star shaped has stellate as an exact synonym.
'Tinged reddish' is a faint red colour. Annotate red, with the tinge as approximate. The examples' context words ('outside', 'with age', 'abaxially') belong to the surface and stage patterns.
The source is one fruit statement ('without vittae or vesicles'). PO has no class for fruit oil vesicles, and the part is unclear without the family context.
Means 2-nerved: a count of veins (vascular bundle PO_0005020), handled like '5-nerved' in the count-of-parts pattern.
A fragment cut off before the covering (hairs, wool). As with 'covered' (C240), the quality is the covering itself.
A narrowly ovate outline is still ovate; 'narrow' only changes the length-to-width ratio. Annotate ovate (a temporary class until pato#627 is merged).

label: obpyramidal
definition: A pyramidal quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being attached at the apex of the pyramid, so that the polygonal base is distal.
reason: A standard shape word for cypselas and seeds. PATO has pyramidal but no inverted form; this parallels obtriangular (FLOPO:0991185) under triangular.
'Stipules ochreate' means the stipules are fused into an ochrea. The ochrea class was added in the previous review.
A faint purple colour spread over the surface. Annotate purple; the suffusion is a weak degree, handled as with 'tinged reddish'.
Means minutely stellate. On hairs and on disc glands it gives the star shape (PATO synonym stellate); the small size is not a separate quality.

target: new: set of parts with mixed values
reason: 'Hairs black and white' means some hairs are black and others white. This is two values over a set of hairs, neither an alternative nor one colour.
Bow-shaped means arcuate, which already maps to curved (rule C185).
The same reading as depressed-globose (C170): a sphere flattened at the poles. 'Sub-' marks the value as approximate.
These tubers, rhizomes and fruits are cylindrical with an uneven outline. 'Irregularly' is a degree word, not a separate quality.
A degree word ('nearly glabrous', 'nearly straight'), the same as ± in the approximate-value pattern. It is not a quality by itself.
'Smell offensive' fits foetid, which is defined as an unpleasant, offensive odour.
An adverb that qualifies the next value ('abruptly acute', 'abruptly differentiated'). It has no meaning on its own.
'Cells 3-4:1' is a length-to-width ratio of the cell, covered by the ratio-of-two-dimensions pattern.
A fragment of 'in loose or dense mats/tufts'. The full phrase already maps to loose (PATO:0001802, rule C169) together with the mat or tuft value.

label: intralaminal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being located within the lamina of a leaf, set in from its margin.
reason: A defined moss term for the position of the limbidium (the leaf's border of differentiated cells). It is the counterpart of marginal (FLOPO:0991208), and nothing in PATO covers it.
Isodiametric cells have a length-to-width ratio of about 1:1, which the 'aspect ratio' item shows these floras state directly. A ratio pattern is better than a new term.
States that the moss capsule has no peristome, and PO has the class peristome.
Multistratose means made of several cell layers, which fits stratified ('exhibiting a layered configuration').
One statement: a negated change in width along the costa, the midrib of a moss leaf. Negating flared would be a doubtful reading, and the negation carries little information.
